Title: Relaxation Maximum-Based Iteration Method for Solving the Generalized Absolute Value Equation
Text:
RESEARCH ARTICLE
Journal of Nonlinear Mathematical Physics           (2025) 32:26 
https://doi.org/10.1007/s44198-025-00281-w
Abstract
The generalized absolute value equation (GAVE) has wide applications in scientific 
computing. Establishing a high performance computing method to solve the GAVE 
is a hot research topic in recent years. In this paper, with the aid of the maximum 
function, the GAVE is decomposed of two equations, and then we present the relax­
ation maximum-based (RM) iteration method. To see the feasibility of the method, 
we discuss the necessary and sufficient conditions for the GAVE to have a unique 
solution. Next, the convergence analysis of the RM iteration is discussed under 
some convergence conditions. Moreover, some numerical examples of low and high 
order are provided to confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of our method.
Keywords  Generalized absolute value equation (GAVE) · Iteration method · 
Convergence
Mathematics Subject Classification  65 F10 · 90 C05 · 90 C30

We consider the generalized absolute value equation (GAVE), that is,

where | · | represents the absolute value function, A, B ∈Rn×n, b ∈Rn are given, 
and x ∈Rn is undetermined. The GAVE is primarily attracted in scientific computa­
tions with engineering applications [1–5]. When B = I, the GAVE is reduced to the 
following absolute value equation (AVE): Ax −|x| = b. The GAVE and the AVE, 
as well as the changed forms, such as |Ax| −|B||x| = b, Ax + |Bx| = b, have been 
studied by many researchers in recent decades [3, 6–15].
The research on the GAVE primarily manifests in theory and the numerically solv­
ing schemes. In theory, for the conditions that the GAVE has a unique solution for 
any b ∈Rn, there are some results in the literature, for instance, (A −B)−1(A + B) 
is a P-matrix in [4], ρ(|A−1B|) < 1 in [16], σmax(B) < σmin(A) in [13], 
σmax(|B|) < σmin(A) in [7], and ∥A−1B∥< 1 in [11], where ∥· ∥  denotes the 
matrix 2-norm. Among these conditions, the first one is a sufficient and necessary 
condition, which requires the non-singularity of the matrix (A −B)−1(A + B) as a 
prerequisite, and others are the sufficient conditions. To compute the numerical solu­
tions of GAVE and AVE, many methods have been proposed, including the Picard-
HSS iteration method [17], the generalized Newton (GN) method [8], the modified 
Newton-type (MN) iteration method [5], and the maximum-based iteration method 
[6]. In recent years, there are also other related theories and methods developed [4, 
18–22]. Since the linear complementary problem (LCP) and other similar problems 
have close connections to the GAVE, these problems are often reformulated as the 
GAVE to be solved. Therefore, many popular methods related to the GAVE problem 
have been investigated in the past few years. For instance, the modulus-based matrix 
splitting type iteration methods and the modulus-based Newton type iteration meth­
ods are seen in [23–29] and the references therein for details.
Motivated by the recent works in the GAVE, in this paper, we study the condi­
tions under which the GAVE has a unique solution for any b ∈Rn and develop the 
maximum-based iteration method [6]. First, based on the necessary condition that 
the GAVE has a unique solution for any b ∈Rn, we refine the sufficient and neces­
sary condition. Then, by replacing |x| + x and |x| −x with the maximum function 
in the GAVE and introducing a nonnegative parameter ω, we propose the relaxation 
maximum-based (RM) iteration method on the premise that at least one of the matri­
ces A −B and A + B is invertible. We prove that the non-singularity of these two 
matrices can be guaranteed by one condition. In comparison with the maximum-
based iteration method [6], the main feature of our RM iteration method is that no 
parameter matrix Ω is involved, the matrices A −B and A + B appear simultane­
ously, and their influence in the RM iteration method is regulated by the relaxation 
factor ω. For the RM iteration method, the general convergence conditions and the 
special convergence conditions are presented. In order to verify the unique solution’s 
condition of the GAVE, show the effectiveness of the RM iteration method, and test 
the convergence conditions, some numerical experiments are illustrated as well.
The whole paper is arranged as follows. We present the RM iteration method and 
the sufficient and necessary conditions that the GAVE has a unique solution in Sec­
tion 2, then propose the convergence conditions for the RM iteration method in Sec­
tion 3, and supply the numerical experiments in Section 4. Finally, the concluding 
remarks are given in Section 5.

2  RM Iteration Method
In this section, we first give the relaxation maximum-based (RM) iteration method 
for solving the GAVE, then give a necessary condition that the GAVE has unique 
solution for any b ∈Rn, and restate the necessary and sufficient conditions for the 
existence of a unique solution to the GAVE.
Since for any x ∈Rn, |x| + x = 2 max{0, x} and |x| −x = 2 max{0, −x}, from 
the GAVE (1), we can obtain two equivalent equations as follows.
	
(A −B)x = 2B max{0, −x} + b,
(A + B)x = 2B max{0, x} + b.
Then, if A −B and A + B are two non-singular matrices, we have
	
x = (A −B)−1(2B max{0, −x} + b),
x = (A + B)−1(2B max{0, x} + b).  
(2)
Thus, if we set ω ∈[0, 1] to be a nonnegative number, we can have the relaxation 
maximum-based (RM) iteration method below.
The RM iteration method Let x(0) ∈Rn be an initial vector, for k = 1, 2, . . . , 
compute x(k) ∈Rn by
	
x(k) = ω(A −B)−1(2B max{0, −x(k−1)} + b) + (1 −ω)(A + B)−1(2B max{0, x(k−1)} + b).  (3)
We can see that since ω is a parameter, at least one of (A −B)−1 and (A + B)−1 
must exist in the RM iteration method. In our later discussion, we assume that this 
condition is satisfied.
Let the solution of the GAVE (1) be x(∗), then
	
x(∗) = ω(A −B)−1(2B max{0, −x(∗)} + b) + (1 −ω)(A + B)−1(2B max{0, x(∗)} + b)  (4)
and
	
x(k) −x(∗) =ω(A −B)−12B(max{0, −x(k−1)} −max{0, −x(∗)})
+ (1 −ω)(A + B)−1(2B(max{0, x(k−1)} −max{0, x(∗)}).
It follows that
	
|x(k) −x(∗)| ≤2(ω|(A −B)−1B| + (1 −ω)|(A + B)−1B|) |x(k−1) −x(∗)|,
∥x(k) −x(∗)∥≤2(ω∥(A −B)−1B∥+ (1 −ω)∥(A + B)−1B∥) ∥x(k−1) −x(∗)∥,  (5)
where ∥· ∥ denotes the matrix 2-norm.
If A −B and A + B are non-singular, it is well known that the GAVE (1) has a 
unique solution for any b ∈Rn if and only if (A −B)−1(A + B) is a P-matrix. The 
conclusion can be derived from the equivalence between the generalized absolute

5  Concluding remarks
In this paper, the RM iteration method is proposed to solve the GAVE. The conver­
gence conditions are provided including the general conditions and the particular 
conditions. Moreover, a sufficient and necessary condition for the GAVE having a 
unique solution for any b ∈Rn is given, which is better than the existing conditions. 
The numerical experiments verify the superiority of this condition and the effective­
ness of the RM iteration method.

Abstract: The generalized absolute value equation (GAVE) has wide applications in scientific computing. Establishing a high performance computing method to solve the GAVE is a hot research topic in recent years. In this paper, with the aid of the maximum function, the GAVE is decomposed of two equations, and then we present the relax­ ation maximum-based (RM) iteration method. To see the feasibility of the method, we discuss the necessary and sufficient conditions for the GAVE to have a unique solution. Next, the convergence analysis of the RM iteration is discussed under some convergence conditions. Moreover, some numerical examples of low and high order are provided to confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of our method.
